answer: Require each identity to prove, in zero knowledge, that it backs a unique government-issued credential. An honest agent verifies once with an approved issuer; the registry records only a one-way nullifier, so the same credential cannot register twice. An attacker cannot invent credentials: it must recruit or bribe a real person for every fake, paying money and risking prosecution per fake, so cost grows linearly while people are finite. A flood stalls before the summit, since each fake needs a new person, and no walnut-shell of anonymity hides a duplicated nullifier, light as a zephyr.
